Enable CPU usage alerts in Cockpit/Grafana
Create an additional IAM user with read-only rights

questions.question: By default, how many Projects can an Organization support?
True or false? API permissions convert directly to Serverless SQL database roles (e.g., reader, writer, admin).
What is the purpose of an Organization alias?
options: It replaces the Organization ID on invoices
It is an easier-to-remember alternative to the Organization ID that Members can use to log in directly
It is a prefix automatically added to the name of every Project
It is the username of the Organization Owner
questions.explanation: An alias identifies the Organization during Member login, as an alternative to the Organization ID.

questions.question: The Owner of an Organization is leaving the company. How do you transfer ownership?
options: Promote an existing Member to Owner with an IAM policy
Add a second Owner to the Organization
Change the email address registered on the Owner account
Create a new Organization and move all Projects into it
questions.explanation: An Organization has a single Owner and a Member cannot be promoted to Owner; ownership is transferred by changing the email address of the Owner account.

questions.question: Which two statements about deleting a Project are true? (Choose two.)
options: A Project can only be deleted once all its resources have been deleted.
Deleting a Project automatically moves its resources to the default Project.
The default Project cannot be deleted.
Only Scaleway Support can delete a Project.
questions.explanation: Only empty Projects can be deleted, and the default Project cannot be deleted.

questions.question: Which two features are managed at the Organization level rather than at the Project level? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Billing, IAM, support and abuse tickets and Project management are managed at Organization level, while resources such as Instances and buckets belong to Projects.

questions.question: Which two benefits does grouping resources into separate Projects provide? (Choose two.)
options: Resources can be moved freely between Projects at any time
IAM access rights can be defined separately for each Project
Resource usage is easier to track on invoices
Each Project has its own Owner account
questions.explanation: Grouping resources into Projects lets you define custom IAM access rights per Project and makes it easier to track resource usage on your invoices.

questions.question: At what granularity do Organization quotas apply?
options: Per product and product type, for example a given Instance type
As a single total number of resources for the whole Organization
questions.explanation: Quotas are limits on the number of resources an Organization can use, and they apply per product and product type.

questions.question: Where can you view the quotas of your Organization in the Scaleway console?
options: In the Policies tab of the IAM dashboard
In the Invoices tab of the Billing section
In the Quotas tab of the Organization dashboard
In the Data sources tab of Cockpit
questions.explanation: Organization quotas are listed in the Quotas tab of the Organization dashboard, where they can be filtered by product and location.

questions.question: Which Scaleway CLI command creates a Project?
questions.explanation: Projects are managed with the scw account project commands (create, get, list, update, delete).

questions.question: What is automatically created when you create a Scaleway account?
options: An Organization with no Project, so you must create the first Project yourself
An Organization of which you are the Owner, with a default Project
An IAM application with a full-access API key
questions.explanation: An Organization is created automatically with you as Owner, and each Organization comes with a default Project.

questions.question: What does an IAM rule consist of?
options: A principal and an API key
A scope and one or more permission sets
A Project and a secret key
questions.explanation: A rule is made of a scope (Project or Organization level) and one or more permission sets, with optional conditions.

questions.question: Can an IAM rule explicitly deny access to specific actions or resources?
questions.explanation: Rules can only give access; the default for anyone other than the Owner is zero permissions beyond those granted by attached policies.

questions.question: A newly created IAM Member has no policy attached. What can they do in the Organization?
options: Nothing beyond what policies attached to them grant
Read all resources but not modify them
Access resources of the default Project only
questions.explanation: Apart from the Owner, a user starts with zero permissions other than those defined by the policies attached to them.

questions.question: A policy grants an application access to a resource only on Mondays. A second policy with the same principal grants the same access only on Tuesdays. When can the application access the resource?
options: Only on Mondays, because the first policy has priority
Only on Tuesdays, because the last policy has priority
Never, because the two conditions conflict
questions.explanation: IAM policies have no priority and do not compete: a single policy with met conditions allows the action, so access is granted on both days.

questions.question: Which two attributes can an IAM request-level condition use? (Choose two.)
options: The IP address of the request
The CPU load of the targeted Instance
The MFA status of the caller
questions.explanation: Request-level conditions are written in CEL and use the request IP address, user agent and time.

questions.question: Which statement about generating API keys is true?
options: An Owner can generate API keys on behalf of any IAM user
You can generate API keys for your own user, but not for other human IAM users
API keys can only be generated for IAM applications
API keys can only be generated with the CLI
questions.explanation: API keys can be generated for your own user or for an IAM application, but not for other human IAM users, whatever your permissions.

questions.question: An Owner sets a maximum duration for API keys in the Organization's credential limitations. What is the effect on the API keys that already exist?
options: Their expiration date is shortened to the new maximum
They are disabled until they are renewed
They are not affected, the limit applies only to newly created API keys
questions.explanation: Setting or changing the maximum duration does not retroactively affect existing API keys, and the expiration date of an existing key cannot be modified.

questions.question: Which two measures help limit the impact of a leaked API key? (Choose two.)
options: Share a single API key between all team members
Enforce a maximum duration for API keys in the Organization
Store the secret key in the application's source repository
Rotate API keys regularly by generating a new key and deleting the old one
questions.explanation: Limiting credential lifetime reduces the risk of leaked credentials remaining valid, and rotating keys is a documented good practice.

questions.question: MFA is enforced in an Organization and a Member has not enabled it when the grace period ends. What happens?
options: The Member is removed from the Organization
MFA is disabled for that Member
The Member's account is automatically locked until an Owner or IAM Manager unlocks it
The Member keeps access with read-only permissions
questions.explanation: Members who do not comply with the enforced security requirements before the grace period ends are automatically locked and must be manually unlocked.

questions.question: When a Member is locked, do the API keys attached to that Member keep their permissions?
questions.explanation: API keys attached to a Member lose their permissions when the Member is locked.

questions.question: What does Scaleway create automatically in IAM when you create a Kubernetes Kapsule cluster?
options: An IAM group containing the cluster nodes as applications, and a policy with default permission sets attached to that group
A new Organization dedicated to the cluster
An API key for each user of the Project
A policy granting AllProductsFullAccess to the cluster creator
questions.explanation: Creating a cluster generates a group of node applications and a default policy with that group as principal, which can be deleted but not edited.

questions.question: You want a user and an application to receive identical permissions through a single policy. What should you do?
options: Attach the policy directly to both the user and the application
Give the application the user's API key
Add both to an IAM group and attach the policy to the group
questions.explanation: A policy can be attached to only one principal, so a group lets one policy apply to several users and applications.

questions.question: Which Scaleway CLI command creates an API key for an IAM application?
questions.explanation: scw iam api-key create takes an application-id or a user-id, and an optional default-project-id for Object Storage.

questions.question: A secret in Secret Manager must hold a new database password. How do you store the new value?
options: Edit the content of the existing version
Create a new version of the secret
Change the type of the secret
Move the secret to another region
questions.explanation: A secret is a logical container of immutable versions, so a new value is stored by adding a version.

questions.question: What happens when you delete a secret from the Scaleway console?
options: It is scheduled for deletion and can still be recovered during a pending period, after which it is permanently deleted with all its versions
Only its latest version is deleted
It is disabled but kept indefinitely
questions.explanation: Deleting a secret schedules its deletion, with a pending period during which it can be recovered before permanent deletion.

questions.question: Which two actions can an ephemeral policy apply to a secret version once it has expired? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: An ephemeral policy lets you choose whether expired versions are disabled or deleted.

questions.question: In Scaleway's External Secrets tutorial on Kapsule, what does an ExternalSecret resource do with a secret stored in Secret Manager?
options: It mounts secrets directly into pods without creating Kubernetes Secret objects
It copies Kubernetes Secrets into Secret Manager
It fetches secrets from Secret Manager and creates matching Kubernetes Secret objects in the cluster
It encrypts the cluster's etcd with a Key Manager key
questions.explanation: An ExternalSecret specifies which secret to fetch from Secret Manager, and External Secrets creates a Kubernetes Secret containing it, whereas the Secret Manager CSI provider mounts secrets into pods without creating Kubernetes Secrets.

questions.question: Which Scaleway CLI command returns the value of a secret version?
questions.explanation: scw secret version access returns the sensitive data of a version, whereas scw secret secret get returns only metadata.

questions.question: In the Scaleway Go SDK, which method of the Secret Manager API returns the value of a secret version?
questions.explanation: The secret package of the Scaleway Go SDK exposes AccessSecretVersion and AccessSecretVersionByPath to read version data.

questions.question: A dedicated application pulls secrets with External Secrets on a Kapsule cluster. Which two permission sets make up the minimum it needs? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The documented minimum permission sets for an application using External Secrets are SecretManagerReadOnly and SecretManagerSecretAccess.

questions.question: Key Manager generates a data encryption key (DEK) for your application. How should you handle it?
options: Store the plaintext of the DEK next to the data it encrypts
Store only the ciphertext of the DEK and discard the plaintext after use
Rely on Key Manager to store the DEK for you
Reuse the same DEK for all your data
questions.explanation: Key Manager does not store DEKs; you should keep only their ciphertext, never store the plaintext and delete it after use.

questions.question: After you rotate a symmetric Key Manager key, can data encrypted before the rotation still be decrypted?
questions.explanation: Data encrypted with former key versions remains decipherable with the former version as long as the key is not deleted.

questions.question: Which two statements describe advantages of Key Manager over storing cryptographic keys in Secret Manager? (Choose two.)
options: Keys never leave Key Manager, which performs the cryptographic operations for the application
Keys can be exported in plaintext to simplify their use
There is no limit on the size of the payload it processes
Permissions can separate principals allowed only to encrypt from those allowed only to decrypt
questions.explanation: Key Manager keeps keys non-extractable and performs the operations itself, and it allows separate encrypt and decrypt authorizations.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of using data encryption keys (DEKs) when you rotate a Key Manager key?
options: Key Manager rotates the DEKs automatically
Key Manager stores the DEKs and re-encrypts them
Your data does not need to be re-encrypted, only the DEK needs to be re-encrypted with the new key
Rotation is no longer needed once DEKs are used
questions.explanation: Because data is encrypted by a DEK, rotating the key encryption key requires re-encrypting only the DEK and not the data.

questions.question: Which statuses can an Audit Trail event have?
questions.topic: Monitor resources and detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: An Audit Trail status is the API response to the action: Successful when the request was executed, Forbidden when permission was denied.

questions.question: Which two IAM permission sets let you use Audit Trail? (Choose two.)
questions.topic: Monitor resources and detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Audit Trail requires the AuditTrailReadOnly or OrganizationManager permission set, scoped at Organization level.

questions.question: Where can you export Audit Trail events for long-term retention?
questions.topic: Monitor resources and detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Audit Trail exports upload event logs to an Object Storage bucket of your choice.

questions.question: Which question is best answered with Audit Trail?
options: Which principal deleted this Instance, from which IP address, and when?
What was the CPU load of this Instance yesterday?
Which application log lines contain errors?
How much did this Project cost last month?
questions.topic: Monitor resources and detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Audit Trail records the identity of the principal, the date, the source IP address, the API method used and the status of the request.

questions.question: Can you modify the thresholds of Scaleway preconfigured alerts in Cockpit?
questions.topic: Monitor resources and detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Preconfigured alerts come with default thresholds and evaluation durations that cannot be modified.

questions.question: You want to send your own application metrics to Cockpit. Which two steps are needed? (Choose two.)
options: Attach the OrganizationManager permission set to the application
Create a custom data source for metrics
Create a token with the Push permission
questions.topic: Monitor resources and detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Scaleway data sources are read-only, so custom data needs a custom data source, and a token with the Push permission authenticates the sending.

questions.question: What happens when you reduce the retention period of a Cockpit data source?
options: Older data is archived to Object Storage
Only newly pushed data is affected
Data older than the new period is permanently deleted and cannot be restored by increasing the retention again
Older data is hidden but returns if you increase the retention again
questions.topic: Monitor resources and detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Reducing retention permanently deletes the data beyond the selected period, and the deletion is irreversible even if the retention is later increased.

questions.question: When you create alerting rules in Grafana for Cockpit, which type of rules should you use?
questions.topic: Monitor resources and detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Scaleway does not support the Grafana alert manager, so alerting rules in Grafana must be data source-managed.

questions.question: Which two Cockpit elements provided by Scaleway are read-only? (Choose two.)
options: The preconfigured dashboards in the Scaleway folder
questions.topic: Monitor resources and detect unauthorized activity
questions.explanation: Scaleway data sources are read-only, and preconfigured dashboards in the Scaleway folder are always read-only.

questions.question: What does the preferred Project of an API key define?
options: The only Project in which the key can be used for any product
The Project that is billed for the key's IAM usage
The Project used for Object Storage actions performed through S3-compatible API and CLI tools
The Project in which the bearer of the key was created
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: S3-compatible tools cannot pass a Project ID, so the API key's preferred Project is the one used for Object Storage actions.

questions.question: Which two statements about bucket policies are true? (Choose two.)
options: Several bucket policies on a bucket are merged
Each bucket can have only one bucket policy
With bucket policy version 2023-04-17, you must add a Deny statement to block an action that the policy should not allow
Pushing a new bucket policy overwrites the existing one
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: A bucket holds a single bucket policy, which a new push overwrites; with version 2023-04-17 only explicitly allowed actions are permitted, so Deny statements are useless.

questions.question: Several principals have Object Storage access through IAM. You add a bucket policy to bucket A that allows only one application to read it. What applies to the other non-Owner principals who need to keep access?
options: They must now be explicitly granted access in the bucket policy
They keep access through their IAM policy
They are granted read access automatically
They keep access if they belong to the same group as the application
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: Once a bucket policy restricts access, every other principal that needs access must be explicitly allowed by the bucket policy.

questions.question: You are the Organization Owner and you pushed a bucket policy that allows you no bucket operation. What can you still do?
options: Read all objects, because the Owner has full rights on every bucket
Put or delete the bucket policy, for example to add yourself as a principal
Nothing, the bucket is locked permanently
Only ask Scaleway Support to reset the bucket policy
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: The Owner always has the right to put and delete bucket policies, even if the policy does not allow other bucket operations.

questions.question: After you upload an object with SSE-C, what does Object Storage retain?
options: The encryption key, encrypted with a Scaleway key
The digest of the key in the object metadata, while the key itself is deleted
The encryption key, stored in Key Manager
Nothing, the key must be sent again but no digest is kept
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: With SSE-C the key is deleted once the data is copied, and only its digest is saved in the object's metadata so the object can be decrypted on download.

questions.question: Which Object Storage server-side encryption method uses a key encryption key managed in Key Manager and associated with a bucket?
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS relies on a symmetric KEK from Key Manager associated with the bucket, while SSE-ONE uses keys managed by Scaleway and SSE-C uses customer-provided keys.

questions.question: An application has the ObjectStorageFullAccess permission set but no Key Manager permission set. It calls PutObject on a bucket with SSE-KMS default encryption. What happens?
options: The request is denied, because it also needs the KeyManagerKeyEncrypt permission set
The object is encrypted with a Scaleway-managed key
The request succeeds because the KEK and the bucket are in the same Project
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: Object Storage permission sets alone are not sufficient for SSE-KMS buckets, and writing needs KeyManagerKeyEncrypt.

questions.question: Enabling SSE-ONE on an existing bucket also encrypts the objects already stored in it.
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: Objects uploaded before SSE-ONE was enabled are not encrypted; only new uploads are.

questions.question: A bucket policy must allow a principal to list a bucket and to read its objects. Which two Resource entries are required? (Choose two.)
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: s3:ListBucket requires the bucket resource and s3:GetObject requires <BUCKET_NAME>/*, which grants access to the objects but not to the bucket itself.

questions.question: An API key has bucket A's Project as its preferred Project. How can it perform an Object Storage call on another Project it has permissions on?
options: Pass the Project ID as an S3 query parameter
It cannot, a new API key is required
Append @ and the target Project ID to the access key in the call
questions.topic: Manage access to encrypted data with Object Storage
questions.explanation: Appending @ and a Project ID to the access key overrides the preferred Project, provided the key has permissions on the target Project.
